finding.expected: Preserve TASK-138 authority and behavior, but make the representative canonical root and manifest path selected for equivalent platform filesystem keys independent of caller/enumeration order. Use a deterministic representative/tie-breaker rather than first-seen setdefault semantics, while keeping absolute resolved paths, overlap deduplication, symlink fail-closed behavior, bounded discovery, exact TASK-125 rehydration, and all M3/M4 boundaries unchanged. Add a focused regression that proves equivalent case spellings on a case-insensitive filesystem key cannot change the returned inventory when root order is reversed; the test may simulate the platform key behavior deterministically where the host filesystem is case-sensitive.
finding.issue: TASK-138 requires root permutation and filesystem aliasing to be deterministic on the platform's canonical filesystem key. The candidate deduplicates equivalent canonical roots and manifests with normcase(...) keys but retains the first raw resolved path via dict.setdefault(...). On a case-insensitive filesystem, two caller spellings of the same physical root/path that differ only by case can map to the same normcase key while preserving different path strings. Because setdefault keeps whichever spelling is encountered first, permuting caller roots can change the representative root and then the emitted manifest_paths text, even though the persisted filesystem state is the same. The focused regression covers overlap and '..' aliases but not case-equivalent aliases, so AC5's root-order independence is not fully enforced.
